newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks shake off weak Dow, end higher.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks shake off weak Dow, end higher.

text.p: Australian stocks shook off a weaker Dow on Thursday, closing up slightly as firmer commodity prices helped a stronger resources sector.
But brokers said many investors remained on the sidelines in fear of what U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan might say in congressional testimony starting later on Thursday.
The All Ordinaries index closed up 6.1 points at 2,391 on reasonable turnover of A$832 million (US$655 million).
Steel, copper and oil group The Broken Hill Pty Co's 24 cent rise to A$17.13 was the key driver.

National Australia Bank, seen as vulnerable to weaker bond markets, closed down 20 cents at A$15.60 after local bond yields rose on fears that Greenspan would talk again about the possibility of a pre-emptive tightening.
"The market's really sitting on its hands, waiting for Greenspan to talk and to see what the Fed does next week," Morgan Stockbroking equities advisor Tony Russell said.

Brokers said firmer metals prices overnight and a reassessment of BHP's recent sharp selloff had helped boost the giant resources group's price. Fellow resource group WMC Ltd also benefitted, closing up seven cents at A$8.16.

Some brokers said there appeared to be some switching out of global minor RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd, which closed down three cents at A$18.42, into BHP. RTZ-CRA announced a major management shake-up on Wednesday.
"There's been a few broker upgrades on BHP too ahead of this quarterly result," said one Sydney dealer. BHP is due to report its third quarter profit results on Friday.
